newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge may face trial over smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge may face trial over smuggling.

text.p: An Argentine congressional commission investigating a smuggling ring said on Monday it had called for the impeachment of a federal judge, local news agencies reported.
The commission accused Judge Carlos Branca of "illegal association" and "bribery" in connection with a so-called "parallel customs" operating in Ezeiza, at the country's international airport.

Commission leader Mario Das Neves, a legislator from the ruling Peronist party, said at a news conference that leaders of Congress' main political blocs had been notified of the impeachment request and supported it.
The request will be considered by Economic Crimes Judge Jorge Brugo, who has ordered three arrests in connection with the case.
Branca told reporters on Monday he was innocent and was willing to be investigated.
Local news agencies said the charges against him were based on a video by a hidden camera showing the judge in a compromising situation.

The government launched an investigation into the customs service last October due to a series of corruption and smuggling scandals it estimates cost $3 billion in uncollected tariffs in the past four years.
